spec.topic: The Killing Ledger — Keddie cabin murders (1981), host-led true-crime documentary

assignedLines.text: Within days, suspicion fell on the neighbor in Cabin 26: Martin Smartt — and his friend, John Boubede.
assignedLines.camera: slow zoom-out with lateral drift combined; sharp, investigative

assignedLines.text: One month later, Smartt told his own therapist he had killed Sue and Tina. The therapist reported it. The state dismissed it as hearsay.
assignedLines.camera: crane-down from high angle to medium; incredulous, tense

assignedLines.text: No arrest. No charges. And Tina? She stayed missing for three long years — until her remains were found sixty-two miles away.
assignedLines.camera: handheld sway, medium close-up; mournful, slow delivery

assignedLines.text: In 2016, a hammer was pulled from the bottom of a nearby pond — matching the one Smartt said went missing that very morning.
assignedLines.camera: push-in, medium to tight close-up; focused, piercing

assignedLines.text: New DNA on the crime-scene tape was said to match a living person known to investigators. And still — nobody has ever been charged.
assignedLines.camera: orbit right, finishing three-quarter front view; frustrated determination

assignedLines.text: Cabin 28 was torn down in 2004. But the questions refuse to die. And on this one — the ledger stays open.
assignedLines.camera: slow pull-back to wide, ending on a static hold; solemn finality
